correctness.rationale: The DIM ↔ vertex bicoloring condition is correctly equivalent to whites having zero white neighbors and blacks exactly one black neighbor. The two coupled cyclic binary equations sum to |X|=|Y|=2n/5. Eliminating y factors the centered recurrence as Φ_3(T)Φ_5(T)z=0. Coprimality and the binary additive-rectangle lemma show every solution is period three or five; white density 2/5 excludes period three. Period-five outer white nonadjacency yields exactly the five shifts of {0,2}; inner colors follow uniquely, and explicit edge residues yield all DIMs. Any 5-color strong edge coloring of a cubic graph has every color once in each 5-edge closed neighborhood, forcing every color class to be a DIM; the only five form the stated partition. Independently implemented exact local binary-equation enumeration for every 5≤n≤20, recovering exactly five for n divisible by 5 and zero otherwise, including wraparound; finite enumeration corroborates universal factorization proof.

(2021) gives broad covering/Petersen-coloring equivalence; none of the materially inspected statements classifies exactly all five DIMs on GP(5m,2) for every m and their resulting rigidity. Newest Karami (2026) quotient-matrix work remains about parameter existence, not realization multiplicities.
